source.title: Weight Initialization and Variance Dynamics in Deep Neural Networks and Large Language Models

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own initialization-scale sweep and compares initialization methods using training outcomes, bearing on initialization’s effect on learning speed and stability. It does not test the original benchmarks or the listed deep-network settings.
record.gate_note: E1 reports qualitative outcomes for three standard-deviation bands; the text does not give per-scale numerical results. E2 reports qualitative comparisons and aggregate statistics over 10 runs, without exact values. E3 tracks weight variance, not training error or the effect of alternative initializations.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's initialization-dependent learning claim in new MNIST and UCI Wine ReLU MLP settings, using controlled scale and initialization comparisons. It does not compare trainable depths.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report a stable initialization-scale band for the MNIST ReLU MLP, faster convergence and lower loss variability with Kaiming than Xavier, and depth-dependent Q/K/V weight-scale equilibration in the transformer. Their proposed explanations for transformer dynamics are interpretations, not experimentally isolated mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses MNIST and UCI Wine ReLU MLPs plus a from-scratch GPT-2–style variance-tracking experiment; it does not use the listed benchmark recipes or depth comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization standard deviation and initialization scheme change reported training behavior in the ReLU MLP experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Kaiming's final validation accuracy matches or slightly exceeds Xavier's.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization choice can affect final validation performance in a fixed ReLU MLP training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Kaiming has lower reported per-epoch loss variability than Xavier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rectifier-aware initialization can reduce reported loss variability during ReLU MLP training.

fits_no_version.finding: Shallow transformer Q/K/V weights expand faster early in training than deeper weights, with eventual layerwise stabilization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer pretraining exhibits depth-dependent weight-scale adaptation.

record.problems: The experiments use MNIST and UCI Wine rather than the claim’s CIFAR benchmarks. E1 and E2 findings are largely qualitative, with no exact accuracy, loss, convergence-time, or variability values in the text. E2 reports 10 runs and a paired t-test p < 0.05, but gives no exact test statistics or effect sizes. E3 reports no numerical layerwise variance values in the text.

untested.parts: CIFAR training classification error, interpolation, corrupted labels, and effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and benefits of extra student neurons.
Depth-related degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.

Greater trainable depth; orthogonal versus matched-variance Gaussian initialization; very deep tanh networks; 10,000-layer convolutional networks. The experiments do not directly establish the proposed signal-propagation mechanism.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth and recovery, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the initial threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on learning speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

missing.what: Figure 2's caption reports higher training accuracy with Kaiming, and Figure 3 reports paired differences in both training loss and training accuracy at p < 0.05 across 10 runs. Record these separately from validation accuracy; exact values, test statistics, and evaluation checkpoints are unspecified.

record.verdict_notes: The findings are largely qualitative. Missing numerical effect sizes limit precision but do not themselves warrant limits_scope. Neither poor results under deliberately unfavorable initialization nor slower Xavier training contradicts V4. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and early stopping or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth-related training error, batch normalization, and the cited special initialization or normalization-free recipes.
Plain-network trainable depth; matched-variance orthogonal versus Gaussian weights; 10,000-layer convolutional networks; and the cited Glorot, He, Schoenholz, Pennington, and Xiao settings.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, squared loss, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization comparisons, speed and learning-rate tolerance across the listed MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet settings, and Fixup.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP (784 → 64 → 32 → 32 → 10)
rows.operation_detail: Train after initializing all linear layers at each of 25 logarithmically spaced standard deviations from 10−4 to 10.
rows.measure: Final accuracy and loss trajectory; updates described as vanishing and accuracy as poor.
rows.value: Extremely small scales (σ ≲ 10−3 ) yield vanishing updates and poor accuracy.
rows.note: The outcome is stated for a range of scales; no per-scale numbers are supplied.
rows.check: Small-scale initialization produces vanishing updates and poor accuracy, as V4 predicts for unfavorable signal propagation. This is supporting evidence, not an incomplete manifestation of V4.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP (784 → 64 → 32 → 32 → 10)
rows.operation_detail: Train after initializing all linear layers at each of 25 logarithmically spaced standard deviations from 10−4 to 10.
rows.measure: Loss trajectory, gradients, and classification accuracy; accuracy peaks within this interval.
rows.value: Training is smooth, gradients remain well-behaved, and accuracy peaks within this interval.
rows.note: The text identifies a stable band but gives no exact accuracy or loss values.
rows.check: The reported stable band gives smooth training and peak accuracy within the fixed schedule. Exact outcomes and directly measured gradient statistics are not supplied.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP (784 → 64 → 32 → 32 → 10)
rows.operation_detail: Train after initializing all linear layers at each of 25 logarithmically spaced standard deviations from 10−4 to 10.
rows.measure: Loss trajectory and classification accuracy; loss is described as unstable with occasional divergence.
rows.value: Very large scales (σ ≳ 1) produce unstable loss and occasional divergence.
rows.note: The text describes instability and occasional divergence, without per-scale numerical results.
rows.check: Instability and occasional divergence at large initialization scales support the predicted consequences of unfavorable initialization; they do not qualify as partial support merely because training fails.

rows.subject: UCI Wine ReLU MLP, Xavier normal
rows.operation_detail: Train with Xavier normal initialization, compared with Kaiming fan-in initialization under identical settings.
rows.measure: Median epochs-to-target and early loss slope; Kaiming has lower median epochs-to-target and steeper early loss slope.
rows.baseline: Kaiming fan-in initialization; median epochs-to-target is lower with Kaiming.
rows.value: Xavier has higher median epochs-to-target and a less steep early loss slope than Kaiming.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison only; no exact epochs-to-target or slopes are given.
rows.check: Xavier's slower convergence relative to rectifier-aware Kaiming is the predicted comparison, not a partial effect. The actual Kaiming distribution is ambiguous: the paper calls it normal but names PyTorch kaiming_uniform in the setup. No numerical convergence times or target specification are reported.

rows.subject: UCI Wine ReLU MLP, Xavier normal
rows.operation_detail: Train with Xavier normal initialization, compared with Kaiming fan-in initialization under identical settings.
rows.measure: Final validation accuracy; Kaiming matches or slightly exceeds Xavier on average.
rows.baseline: Kaiming fan-in initialization; final validation accuracy matches or slightly exceeds Xavier on average.
rows.value: Xavier final validation accuracy matches or is slightly below Kaiming on average.
rows.uncertainty: Paired t-tests show significant differences in training accuracy (p < 0.05); exact accuracy values and direction-specific test statistics not stated.
rows.note: The text reports final validation accuracy qualitatively and separately reports significance for training accuracy.
rows.check: Final validation accuracy alone does not measure learning speed or trainable depth. The cited p < 0.05 concerns training accuracy and loss, not validation accuracy. The Kaiming normal-versus-uniform implementation discrepancy also applies.

rows.subject: UCI Wine ReLU MLP, Xavier normal
rows.operation_detail: Train with Xavier normal initialization, compared with Kaiming fan-in initialization under identical settings.
rows.measure: Per-epoch loss variability; Kaiming is described as more stable, with lower loss variability than Xavier.
rows.baseline: Kaiming fan-in initialization has lower loss variability than Xavier.
rows.value: Xavier has higher loss variability than Kaiming.
rows.note: The text gives no numerical loss variability.
rows.check: Per-epoch loss variability alone does not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth. It is an ancillary stability result. The paper does not clearly distinguish variability along a declining loss trajectory from variability around that trajectory; the Kaiming distribution is also inconsistently specified.

rows.subject: 12-transformer GPT-2–style model
rows.operation_detail: Track standard deviations of attention Q/K/V weights by layer during pretraining.

conditions.value: normal distribution, std 0.02 for most modules and Xavier normal for embedding matrix

rows.measure: Layerwise Q/K/V weight standard deviation over training; lower layers expand rapidly and pronouncedly early, higher layers more slowly and smoothly, and each layer eventually stabilizes around a narrow variance band.
rows.value: Depth-dependent variance dynamics and eventual stabilization are reported.
rows.note: This measures weight-variance dynamics, not the initialization effect on learning speed or trainable depth named in the claim versions.
rows.check: Correctly excluded: weight standard deviations across transformer layers do not measure initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth, and no alternative initialization is tested.

relationships.condition: MNIST ReLU MLP, Adam at learning rate 0.01, fixed 10-epoch initialization-scale sweep
relationships.reason: E1-small, E1-stable, and E1-large report poor learning at tiny scales, smooth learning in the intermediate band, and instability at large scales, supporting initialization-dependent learning.
relationships.display_finding: Tiny initialization scales produced poor learning, intermediate scales produced smooth learning, and large scales produced instability.

relationships.condition: UCI Wine ReLU MLP, Xavier versus Kaiming fan-in across 10 runs
relationships.reason: E2-speed reports lower median epochs-to-target and steeper early loss decline with Kaiming. The qualitative speed advantage supports V4, although the Kaiming distribution is inconsistently specified.
relationships.display_finding: Kaiming fan-in reduced median epochs to target and steepened early loss decline relative to Xavier.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ReLU MLP initialization-scale sweep on MNIST
reader_labels.reason: The reported stable learning band and poor or unstable outcomes at very small or very large scales show initialization scale affects learning behavior (E1-small, E1-stable, E1-large). This does not test the version’s depth claims or its specific initialization comparisons.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Kaiming is reported to converge faster and with lower loss variability than Xavier, while final validation accuracy is comparable or slightly better (E2-speed, E2-accuracy, E2-variance).
